correctness.rationale: The stationary Poisson backward age has density r e^{-ra}. Integrating the Gamma maturation CDF against the phase-locked square-wave signal and taking its first Fourier harmonic gives A/(4q/pi)=[x/sqrt(x^2+w^2)] [(1+x/k)^2+(w/k)^2]^(-k/2), valid for all k,w,x>0 by Tonelli/Fubini. Differentiating log amplitude and multiplying positive denominators produces exactly the stated quartic P; independently verified symbolically with SymPy. Coefficients have exactly one positive-to-negative sign variation for all k>0 (including 0<k<1,1<=k<2 and k>=2), and P(0)<0,P(infty)>0, giving a unique global peak. The derivative ∂_k(k(k+x)/((k+x)^2+w^2))=[x(k+x)^2+(2k+x)w^2]/denom^2>0, independently verified, proves that increasing shape moves the unique root left. The rescalings x~w^(2/3) and x~w/sqrt(k), expansion a=(1/k-1)/3, leading amplitude constant and deterministic x(x^2+w^2)=w^2 are obtained by balancing polynomial powers. Finite symbolic/numeric tests support, not substitute for, these universal deductions.
residual_risks: The result models one ideal phase-selected observable, not a full smooth double-well Langevin trajectory; Gamma marks must be aborted at each reset.

value.rationale: Exact rate-optimization and response-exponent laws distinguish heterogeneous maturation from deterministic delay in a natural renewal-response observable. The full positive shape continuum and monotonic preference ordering are mathematically informative, providing a sharp parametric resonance classification rather than another mere numerical optimum.
residual_risks: Idealized two-branch model does not imply analogous resonance for every real active-matter potential or every forcing harmonic.

final_claim: In the explicitly defined phase-selected Poisson reset response with independent Gamma(k,tau/k) maturation marks aborted upon new resets, the first-harmonic amplitude has one unique globally optimal positive reset rate for every positive forcing frequency and real shape k>0, decreasing strictly in k at fixed mean, with sharp low/high frequency asymptotics and a singular deterministic-latency limit.
limitations: Positive angular frequency, k,tau>0 and reset rate r>0; q amplitude positive and no interactions between reset marks.
The r=0 continuation is mathematical, not a stationary Poisson process with zero rate.
